method: peer positions derived live from OUR Fluree ledger's ex:SyndicateParticipation nodes (the six filed commitment schedules, Task 8), keyed on the counterparty's real GLEIF LEI and confirmed against ccf_v2.facility. Bank of America discloses an exact figure; Citibank discloses only the band from a fixed published ladder that contains its position -- the ladder is a lookup, not a function of the figure, so it narrows nothing. The peer's internal rating and workout posture use the SNC programme's coarse regulatory categories, deliberately not our notch grades: the peer is less precise than we are, and that is what makes the boundary visible. Product declarations (Task 15) are the three §F conditions that sound like runtime behaviour -- a request that times out, a claim nobody attested, a remote TTL shorter than ours -- represented as declarations in data. The SDK reads and acts on them; this project never does.

declarations.note: baseline: fast (well under the 5s bound), attested, TTL at 6h (above the 4h local composite) -- the contrast case for both the timeout floor and the TTL floor. Without this row, every declaration would be slow or short-TTL and neither floor would prove anything.

engineered to breach the default 5s max_federation_latency bound (§B) so fail-closed is observed rather than merely described. Still attested -- it is the LATENCY floor's contrast case, not the attestation floor's.

engineered unattested claim (attestation IS NULL) with a sub-4h TTL, so both the attestation floor and the 'TTL below the local composite' floor bind on one row. Fast latency on purpose -- it must not also be the timeout contrast, or the three floors stop being independently demonstrated.
